seo.title: What is uptime monitoring?
seo.description: Uptime monitoring is an external service that checks your site at intervals and alerts someone when it stops answering correctly.

definition: Uptime monitoring is an external service that checks your site at intervals and alerts someone when it stops answering correctly.
answerBlock: Uptime monitoring is an external service that checks your site at intervals and alerts someone when it stops answering correctly. The point is that you hear about an outage before a customer telephones about it. Good monitoring checks a real journey, not only whether the front page returns a response.

body.heading: What should monitoring actually check?
paragraphs: More than the homepage. A site can return a perfectly healthy front page while the checkout is broken, the contact form is failing silently or the search index is empty. Checks should cover the journeys that earn money.
It should also watch the things that fail quietly: certificate expiry, a queue that has stopped processing, disk filling up, and error rates rising without the site going down.
Alerts need an owner and a route. An alert that reaches an unread mailbox is monitoring theatre.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: The cost of downtime is not only lost orders. It is the enquiries that never arrive and are never counted, and the buyers who conclude you are not a serious supplier.
Monitoring evidence also makes a support agreement measurable rather than a matter of opinion about how often things break.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: A care plan monitors the site, the form submissions and the background queue, so a failed email job raises an alert rather than sitting unnoticed until someone asks where their confirmation went.

service.title: Website care plans
service.line: Patching, backups with a tested restore, monitoring and a fixed allowance of development hours.

terms.definition: A backup is a copy of the site and its database held somewhere else, and a restore is the rehearsed process of putting that copy back.
A content delivery network is a set of servers spread around the world that serve copies of your files from somewhere near each visitor.
DNS is the system that turns a domain name someone types into the address of the server that answers for it.
A staging environment is a private copy of the live site where changes are tested before anyone outside the company sees them.
